title: Frontend: Undo Redo
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Undo Redo. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Controlled Text input starts empty. Each edit commits a new history state. Undo and Redo navigate history with disabled boundary buttons. Editing after undo discards future history. Output [data-testid=current] mirrors current text.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
alternativeApproaches: Group a drag or typing burst into one undoable transaction rather than hundreds of snapshots.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Undo at start; redo at end; undo then new edit.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
